artworks.title: The Origin of the Milky Way
artworks.description: An oil painting by the Venetian master Tintoretto, now in the National Gallery, London. It depicts the myth in which Jupiter holds the infant Heracles to the breast of the sleeping Juno (Hera) so that the child may gain immortality; the milk that sprays upward from the startled goddess forms the Milky Way. The composition's swirling diagonals and tumbling putti are characteristic of Tintoretto's late dynamic style.

artworks.title: The Campana Hera
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Greek original
artworks.description: A monumental marble statue of Hera, a Roman copy of the second century AD after a Greek original. The goddess stands veiled and crowned with a diadem, an image of regal, matronly dignity befitting the queen of Olympus. Named after the Campana collection from which it was acquired, the statue is now in the Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: The Birth of the Milky Way
artworks.description: Painted for the Torre de la Parada hunting lodge of Philip IV of Spain and now in the Museo del Prado, Rubens's Baroque treatment of the same myth Tintoretto had staged: Jupiter presses the infant Heracles to the breast of the sleeping Juno, and the spray of divine milk that starts up becomes the Milky Way. Hera is the startled axis of the composition — queen, stepmother, and cosmic fountain — rendered with the fleshy energy and swirling putti of Rubens's late mythological cycle.

artworks.title: Hera Hiding during the Battle of the Gods and Giants
artworks.description: A rare mythological canvas by Carel Fabritius, Rembrandt's gifted pupil, now in the Pushkin Museum, Moscow. While the Gigantomachy rages, Hera draws her mantle close and turns aside — the queen of the gods caught not in triumph but in wary withdrawal. The quiet, half-shadowed figure stands apart from the usual Baroque storm of Olympian combat, an intimate psychological reading of the goddess who so often directs myth from the edge of the fray.

artworks.title: The Hera Farnese
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Greek original of the Ephesus-Vienna type
artworks.year: 1st century AD (copy); Greek original 4th century BC
artworks.description: A Roman Imperial marble statue of Hera from the Farnese Collection, now in the Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli (inv. 6027). Of the Ephesus-Vienna type after a Greek Classical original of the fourth century BC, the goddess stands veiled and diademed in the severe matronly pose that became the canonical image of Olympian queenship. Once displayed among the Farnese antiquities in Rome, it remains one of the most widely reproduced sculptural portraits of Hera in the Western tradition.

films.title: Hercules
films.description: Disney softens the queen of the gods into a warm stepmother — a deliberate rewrite of the jealous Hera of the labours — so the film's real antagonist can be Hades instead.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: On Harryhausen's Olympus, Hera is Jason's quiet patron, tipping the divine scales while Zeus looks on — the goddess of marriage as a player in the Argonaut game.

films.title: Hercules: The Legendary Journeys
films.description: Syndicated Hercules made Hera the hero's relentless stepmother: statues that crush, monsters she looses, and a queen of the gods who never forgives Zeus's favorite bastard.

films.title: Blood of Zeus
films.description: Netflix's animated Olympus keeps Hera as Zeus's wounded, political queen — marriage, vengeance and divine realpolitik braided through the war over their world.

films.title: Kaos
films.description: Covell's Netflix black comedy casts Hera as Olympus's sharp-tongued first lady — the goddess of marriage watching Zeus's crumbling rule with a glass of something stronger than nectar.

music.title: The Golden Apple
music.description: A through-sung Broadway retelling of the Judgement of Paris set in turn-of-the-century Washington state: Hera, Athena and Aphrodite compete for a golden apple at an angel-food bake-off.

music.title: Semele
music.description: Handel gives Juno the opera's sharpest edge: the queen of the gods engineers Semele's ruin with jealousy, disguise and a single fatal wish — Hera as baroque strategist.

music.title: Il pomo d'oro
music.description: Cesti's Viennese festa teatrale stages the Judgement of Paris: Hera among the three goddesses competing for the golden apple that will light the road to Troy.

music.title: La Calisto
music.description: Cavalli's Giunone storms through the Venetian comedy as the wronged wife hunting Jupiter's nymph — Hera's jealousy set to some of the seventeenth century's most vivid dramatic music.

popCulture.title: Wonder Woman Historia: The Amazons
popCulture.creator: Kelly Sue DeConnick
popCulture.description: DeConnick's DC Black Label epic opens with Hera's rage and the forging of the Amazons — the queen of the gods as the mythic engine behind Wonder Woman's people.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's sequel brings Hera among the Olympian boon-givers: the goddess of marriage offers frost and family barbs as Melinoë fights Chronos.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's Camp Half-Blood keeps Hera as the goddess of family who can bless or curse a demigod's road — queen of Olympus in a series that made the pantheon teenage reading.

popCulture.title: Lore Olympus
popCulture.creator: Rachel Smythe
popCulture.description: Smythe's Webtoon redraws Hera as Olympus's long-suffering, stylish queen — marriage vows, side-eyes and divine gossip in a pastel retelling centred on Persephone and Hades.

popCulture.title: Age of Mythology
popCulture.creator: Ensemble Studios
popCulture.description: Ensemble's strategy epic offers Hera among the Greek major gods: Olympian favour as a build path, her myth units and technologies backing a player's Bronze Age war.
